clue.text: Feeble way to get name back

parts.note: a path is a way or track

indicators.note: back tells us the word for name is read in reverse order

parts.note: to cite someone is to name them

explanation.surface: Someone finds it pitiful that they have to go some route just to recover a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a feeble or pitiful effort is a woeful, pathetic one.

clue.text: Sanctimonious expression of contempt about Diana?

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes round the actress's surname

parts.note: pish is an exclamation of scorn
Diana Rigg was the actress who played Emma Peel in The Avengers

explanation.surface: A holier-than-thou sneer aimed at someone called Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Diana is a famous bearer of the name, the actress Diana Rigg.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a prig is smugly self-righteous, so sanctimonious is priggish.

clue.text: Discussing business in useless forum

definitions.meaning: a body that debates endlessly without acting

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both conversation about work and a disparaging name for an assembly that only chatters.

clue.text: Magical fish, having lost head, placed first bet

indicators.note: having lost head means the fish's first letter is dropped

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
to ante is to place a stake before the deal in poker

explanation.surface: A gambler's tale of an enchanted fish and an opening wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something under a spell is bewitched or magical.

clue.text: Resistance breaks into a few bars to start with

definitions.text: a few bars to start with

indicators.note: breaks into means the resistance letter forces its way inside the word that follows

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Resistance fighters break in, as music plays its opening bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks into' puts R inside INTO, between T and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction to a song is its opening passage of a few bars.

clue.text: Fish listen to ship going past

indicators.note: the ship's letters pass round either side of the word for listen, enclosing it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
hark is an old word meaning listen

explanation.surface: An instruction to hear the fish as a vessel sails by.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharks are a large group of predatory fish, so fish here is a general class term.

clue.text: Had ambitions for his first comment piece

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of his

parts.note: an op-ed is a newspaper opinion article opposite the editorial page

explanation.surface: A columnist aimed high with his first opinion article.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have hoped for something is to have aspired to it.

clue.text: Old port and whisky

definitions.meaning: ... in Sussex was one of the Cinque Ports, a medieval group of English coastal towns

explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as a wine beside whisky; here it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sussex town was a historic harbour, and the same word names an American whiskey style.

clue.text: Locates from opposite sides

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something found by approaching from both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to site something is to place or locate it.

clue.text: Release boy carrying round sponge

parts.note: to free is to release

indicators.note: carrying means the boy holds the round letter inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Free a boy who is holding a round sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponge' looks like a bath item but is the verb for living off others.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sponge is to take from others without paying your share.

clue.text: Banned guilds policed city centres

indicators.note: centres asks for the central letters of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Craft guilds once patrolled a city and banned things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centres' takes IL from guilds, LIC from policed and IT from city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something banned is forbidden by law, which is what illicit means.

clue.text: Extremely poor pastries found in rubbish

indicators.note: found in places the pastries inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
pies are pastries

explanation.surface: Pastries discovered in the bin are of very low quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is informal British for poor in quality, and the superlative means the very worst.

clue.text: To strike out on his own, eccentric theologian has to waste hours

definitions.text: To strike out on his own

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
has to waste means the letter for hours must be thrown away from the theologian

explanation.surface: A quirky divine decides to go solo but squanders time doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to waste' removes H from THEOLOGIAN, leaving TEOLOGIAN, which 'eccentric' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to strike out on one's own is to act independently, without help.

clue.text: They all died taking too many drugs during parties

indicators.note: during puts the overdose within the parties

parts.note: dos are parties, as in a leaving do
OD is short for overdose

explanation.surface: A grim tale of revellers overdosing at parties and all dying.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests partygoers; the definition is the extinct birds, which all died out.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the dodo is the classic extinct bird, so every one of them perished.

clue.text: Challenges South Africa with a hit outside capital

parts.note: dares are challenges

indicators.note: outside puts the word for hit around the letter a

parts.note: to lam is to beat or hit

explanation.surface: South Africa is challenged with a smash beyond the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dar es Salaam is the largest city of Tanzania and was long its capital.

clue.text: Sense good deal

definitions.meaning: one of the five senses, vision
a ... more means a good deal more, a large amount

explanation.surface: Sensible advice to strike a fair bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is a sense, and informally a sight can mean a great quantity.

clue.text: Fish leave first, wearing hats

indicators.note: wearing means the boaters go round that letter like a hat on a head

parts.note: boaters are flat straw hats

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of leave

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave early with your hat on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are herrings cured whole by salting and smoking, so they are a kind of fish.

clue.text: Maybe bitter about chaotic puzzle

indicators.note: about means the beer wraps around the word for chaotic

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer, hence maybe
wild means unruly or chaotic

explanation.surface: A sour remark about a messy puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a hoppy British ale, which is why the clue hedges with 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to puzzle someone is to confuse or baffle them.

clue.text: It haunts me, somehow, to ignore American composer

indicators.note: somehow means the remaining letters are arranged in some new way
to ignore means the American letter is left out of the phrase

explanation.surface: A composer's melody haunts the speaker, though not an American one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' drops A from IT HAUNTS ME, and 'somehow' rearranges ITHUNTSME.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunesmith is an informal word for a writer of popular songs.

clue.text: Sad inventor gets flower

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone

explanation.surface: A gloomy inventor is given a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the bluebell is a spring woodland flower.

clue.text: Fish had debts tracked

parts.note: the shad is a herring-like fish
to have owed is to have had debts

explanation.surface: A fish in debt was followed by its creditors.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to shadow someone is to follow them closely and secretly.

clue.text: Sound quality of Davidson as a leader

indicators.note: of here means made from part of the following words, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Praise for the tone of a man named Davidson in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal voice is a quality of sound produced through the nose.

clue.text: Spill one records

definitions.meaning: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting a fire

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spill' looks like a verb but is the noun for a thin lighting strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a slender candle or spill, and also, as a jokey agent noun, someone who tapes.

clue.text: Folds unable to move with head down

indicators.note: head down sends the first letter of a down answer to the bottom

parts.note: stuck means unable to move

explanation.surface: Someone frozen with head bowed, folded over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head down' moves the S of STUCK to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tucks are folds stitched into fabric.

clue.text: Bring up fish in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as heard when spoken

parts.note: rays are flat fish

explanation.surface: Mentioning fish while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' suggests mentioning a topic, but here means rearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bring up children is to raise them.

clue.text: What MPs do as a member hasn't turned up yet

parts.note: a leg is a limb or member of the body
something that has not arrived yet is late

explanation.surface: An MP misses parliamentary work by turning up late.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs are Members of Parliament, which makes 'member' look like part of the definition; here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawmaking: Members of Parliament pass laws, which is what it means to legislate.

clue.text: Mentor first to give you fish

indicators.note: first to takes the opening letter of give

parts.note: U is text-speak for you
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A mentor's first move is to give you a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mentor advises and steers, as a guide does.

clue.text: Drug fish with a German drug

parts.note: the cod is a common fish
ein is German for a
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone sedates a fish along with a German drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate painkiller, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Outstanding battle isn't finished

indicators.note: isn't finished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a duel is a fight between two

explanation.surface: An unresolved fight remains outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like excellent, but means owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unpaid outstanding bill is still owed.

clue.text: University worried by international copy

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
ate means troubled or worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A university is troubled by an international copy of its work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to copy someone's manner is to mimic them.

clue.text: Understand the German garden tool

parts.note: to see is to understand
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Grasping what a German gardening implement is.
explanation.definitionFit: A seeder is a device for sowing seed, used in a garden.

clue.text: Persist with ruminant drinking hot sauce

parts.note: to be is to exist or continue

indicators.note: drinking means the camel takes in the letter for hot

parts.note: a camel chews the cud, so it is a ruminant
H stands for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Keep going with a camel slurping hot sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Béchamel is a classic white sauce made with milk and roux.
